fatal_errors: The proposed SiC addition and approximately 1700 °C reactive sintering do not reconstruct the target intervention: a 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder consolidated by spark plasma sintering, optimally at 1500 °C.

The claimed in-situ silica/borosilicate grain-boundary phase under inert sintering conditions is not established by the cited evidence and lacks a specified oxygen or oxide source and reaction pathway.

The sole citation concerns high-entropy diboride hardness and oxidation testing and provides no support for SiC-assisted sintering, silica/borosilicate formation, or liquid-plating-metal corrosion resistance.

The experiment confounds composition and processing temperature by comparing a lower-temperature composite only against high-temperature pure ZrB2, rather than including matched pure-ZrB2 and SiC-containing controls at the same processing temperature.

The liquid-metal bath composition, temperature, exposure duration, and quantitative corrosion metric are unspecified, preventing comparison with the target molten-Al exposure at 700 °C for up to 12 days.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad need for lower-temperature processing, mechanical integrity, oxidation resistance, and liquid-metal durability, but it proposes a scientifically different and inadequately supported intervention. It misses the high-entropy-alloy binder, SPS pressure/heating/hold schedule, 1500 °C optimum, liquid-binder pore filling and grain bonding, and the deterioration at 1600 °C from binder loss. Its outcomes are qualitative and omit the target density, hardness, toughness, molten-Al corrosion-rate, and wear predictions. Although the proposed experiment is nominally falsifiable and includes microscopy, mechanical, oxidation, and corrosion measurements, it lacks matched controls, density/body-quality measurements, defined service conditions, and a processing-temperature series capable of identifying an optimum. SiC modification of ZrB2 is also a familiar strategy rather than a strongly novel hypothesis, and the supplied evidence does not validate its central mechanism.
